subject: Re: Marketplace listing fee realignment — Ops & finance action plan
messages:
From: Anna Morales <anna@aws-partner.amazon.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@aws-partners.com>, AWS Marketplace Ops <mktplace-ops@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming AWS Marketplace listing fee changes (effective Oct 1)

Hi Vivek,

Quick heads up from our side — AWS is rolling a refresh to Marketplace listing fees and the partner contribution model effective Oct 1. Overall the headline: a new per-listing handling fee plus adjustments to co-sell credit bands.

Summary (short):
- New handling fee: $0.35 per listing event (applies to cross-region catalog updates)
- Reduced promo credit for first-year listings (from 10% -> 6%)
- Opportunity: targeted credits for high-volume co-sell partners in Q4 (case-by-case)

I attached the internal fee pivot doc (pdf) and a proposed merchant notice. We know this can shift economics for customers listed through the marketplace; happy to jump on a call to walk through the line items and discuss transition options (temporary waivers, amortized adjustments, or merchant credits).

If you can loop in finance and procurement we'll surface the specific line items that matter to Redwood. Samir and I can be available tomorrow afternoon for a 30-min sync.

Best,
Anna Morales
Partner Programs — AWS Marketplace
anna@aws-partner.amazon.com

Attachment: aws_marketplace_fee_notice_sept2027.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming AWS Marketplace listing fee changes (effective Oct 1)

Team —

Forwarding the note from AWS (below). Immediate ask: can finance and partnerships quantify net ARR / gross margin impact for the current FY if these fees land as-is? Key things I want in the first-pass analysis by EOD:

1) Delta to cost of goods sold (COGS) per customer by SKU (use the same SKU mapping from our Q2 Marketplace report).
2) Impact to co-sell economics (gross margin and expected credit loss if promo goes from 10% to 6%).
3) Suggested mitigation playbook (waiver ask, 2-quarter amortization of fee for existing listings, or marketing credits).
4) Procurement steps: who needs to be engaged (legal, procurement, accounting) and any PO/DocuSign windows we need to respect.

Marissa — can you populate the pivot in the drive link I just created? I started a quick model (aws_fee_pivot_v2.xlsx) with placeholder volume assumptions. Rishi — flag any accounting recognition issues; do we need an accrual or reserve? Laura — if you could surface any contractual SOWs that reference Marketplace economics, that'd help.

I'll reply to AWS with a short list of follow-ups and propose a call Thursday 11am PT.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment: aws_fee_pivot_v2.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming AWS Marketplace listing fee changes (effective Oct 1)

Vivek / team —

I pulled rough numbers into the pivot. High level: if we assume our Q3 marketplace volume holds, the new per-listing handling fee looks like a $28k run-rate increase (US listings only) and ~0.7 pts of gross margin compression. Details in the sheet.

Negotiation playbook ideas:
- Ask for a staggered implementation: waive handling fee for existing listings for 6 months, then 50% in Q1.
- Request preservation of the 10% promo credit for Redwood for all listings created before Oct 1 (retroactive grandfathering).
- Seek a Q4 targeted co-sell uplift credit tied to agreed pipeline milestones (this is non-standard but AWS has offered case-by-case credits in the past).

I can run a more conservative sensitivity (low/mid/high volume) if useful. Recommend we escalate to legal early — marketplace contract language can be subtle. Also propose a short external message to customers (ops + comms) if we expect material price-visible changes.

Marissa
Director, GTM Partnerships

Attachment: aws_fee_pivot_v2.xlsx (updated)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming AWS Marketplace listing fee changes (effective Oct 1)

Quick finance read:
- The $0.35 handling fee will need to be expensed as a direct cost tied to marketplace revenue; we should track it to a new GL code (MarketFees-2027) so we can view P&L impact cleanly.
- If we negotiate a waiver/credit it's best to capture as a contra-revenue / credit memo. For accounting we need explicit language from AWS that outlines credit timing and conditions.
- Procurement/Legal: if we sign any MOU / temporary waiver, route it through procurement for signature authority > $25k. Also check our existing marketplace addendum for any termination/fee-change clause — Laura can you confirm where that sits?

Action items for me: I will draft the budget note and update the monthly financial forecast (need the high/mid/low pivots by EOD). If we cannot get a waiver, suggest we amortize the first two quarters of estimated fee into Q4 marketing spend to minimize headline guide impact.

Rishi
VP, Finance Operations

Attachment: procurement_notes_0901.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Anna Morales <anna@aws-partner.amazon.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@aws-partners.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Upcoming AWS Marketplace listing fee changes (effective Oct 1) — Redwood ask and MAP

Anna / Samir —

Thanks for the heads up. We appreciate the context and the willingness to discuss targeted credits. To keep this moving, here is our proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

1) AWS to provide a line-item invoice sample showing the new handling fee and how it will be billed (by 2027-09-03).
2) AWS to confirm whether existing Redwood listings can be grandfathered at 10% promo credit for 6 months or if a retroactive credit can be issued (answer by 2027-09-04).
3) Redwood to provide a short model (low/mid/high) for expected listing events and P&L impact (shared).
4) If a waiver/credit is agreed, AWS legal to send a 30-day temporary MOU / waiver via DocuSign for signature; Redwood procurement will review within 48 hours.

We would like to propose a Thursday 11am PT call to review the sample invoice and draft waiver. Marissa and Rishi will lead on the numbers; Laura will spot any contract language. Vanessa will coordinate comms if we need to notify customers.

Anna — can you confirm availability for Thu 11am PT and attach the invoice sample? Also please share the appropriate legal contact for the waiver.

If the above is acceptable we can avoid a disruptive customer-facing change and keep quarterly guidance stable.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Links: https://www.docusign.net/temporary-mou/aws-waiver-2027
